concepts.name: Hooks as function component features
concepts.summary: Recall that hooks are special functions starting with 'use' that let function components hold state and use React features without classes.

concepts.name: Rules of Hooks
concepts.summary: Explain that hooks must be called only at the top level of components or custom hooks, never inside conditions, loops or nested functions.

concepts.name: useState state variable and setter
concepts.summary: Understand that useState returns the current value and a setter function, and that calling the setter triggers a re-render.

concepts.name: State persists between renders
concepts.summary: Explain that state is kept by React across renders while ordinary local variables are reset on every call.

concepts.name: Initial state value
concepts.summary: Recall that the argument to useState is used only on the first render to set the initial value.

concepts.name: Controlled inputs with state
concepts.summary: Understand how an input's value and onChange handler are tied to a state variable.

misconceptions.text: Changing a state variable directly, such as count = count + 1, updates the screen.
Hooks can be called anywhere in a component, including inside if statements or loops.
Hooks only work in class components or are just a replacement syntax for this.state.

concepts.name: Functional state updates
concepts.summary: Apply the form setState(prev => next) when the new state depends on the previous state.

concepts.name: Immutable updates of objects and arrays
concepts.summary: Update object and array state by creating new copies with spread or array methods rather than mutating in place.

concepts.name: useEffect for side effects
concepts.summary: Use useEffect to run side effects such as fetching data or updating the document title after render.

concepts.name: Dependency array behaviour
concepts.summary: Choose no array, an empty array or a list of values to control when an effect re-runs.

concepts.name: Effect cleanup functions
concepts.summary: Return a cleanup function from an effect to remove subscriptions, timers or listeners.

concepts.name: Lazy state initialisation
concepts.summary: Pass a function to useState so an expensive initial value is computed only on the first render.

concepts.name: useRef for mutable values and DOM nodes
concepts.summary: Use useRef to hold a value that persists without causing re-renders or to access a DOM element.

misconceptions.text: Calling setState updates the variable immediately, so the next line sees the new value.
Pushing onto a state array and then calling the setter with the same array will trigger a re-render.
useEffect with an empty dependency array runs on every render.

concepts.name: Stale closures in hooks
concepts.summary: Analyse how event handlers and effects capture the values from the render in which they were created, and fix stale values.

concepts.name: Exhaustive dependencies
concepts.summary: Determine the correct dependency list for an effect and restructure code instead of suppressing the lint rule.

concepts.name: Data fetching in effects
concepts.summary: Implement fetching in useEffect with loading and error state and guard against race conditions using cleanup or abort signals.

concepts.name: useReducer state machines
concepts.summary: Use a reducer and dispatched actions to manage state with several related transitions.

concepts.name: useContext for shared values
concepts.summary: Provide a value with a context provider and read it in descendants with useContext, avoiding prop drilling.

concepts.name: Writing custom hooks
concepts.summary: Extract reusable stateful logic into functions beginning with 'use' that compose built-in hooks.

concepts.name: Effects versus event handlers
concepts.summary: Distinguish logic that belongs in event handlers or render calculation from logic that truly needs an effect to synchronise with an external system.

concepts.name: Derived state versus stored state
concepts.summary: Decide when a value should be computed during render from existing state or props rather than stored in separate state.

misconceptions.text: Omitting a dependency from the array is fine because the effect will always see the latest values anyway.
Syncing props into state with an effect is the normal way to compute derived values.
Two components using the same custom hook share the same state.

concepts.name: Memoization with useMemo and useCallback
concepts.summary: Analyse when caching a computed value or function identity preserves referential equality and actually avoids work.

concepts.name: React.memo and referential stability
concepts.summary: Trace how unstable object and function props defeat React.memo and decide which stabilisations are needed.

concepts.name: Evaluating optimisation cost
concepts.summary: Judge by measurement with the profiler whether memoization is worth its complexity or if restructuring components is better.

concepts.name: Context performance and splitting
concepts.summary: Evaluate how context value changes re-render all consumers and choose splitting, memoised values or state colocation in response.

concepts.name: Imperative handles with refs
concepts.summary: Use ref forwarding and useImperativeHandle to expose a limited imperative API from a child component.

concepts.name: Layout effects and timing
concepts.summary: Analyse the render, commit, layout effect and passive effect order to choose useLayoutEffect for DOM measurement before paint.

concepts.name: External stores with useSyncExternalStore
concepts.summary: Subscribe to non-React state sources safely so that concurrent rendering does not show inconsistent values.

concepts.name: Strict Mode double invocation
concepts.summary: Interpret why Strict Mode re-runs renders and effects in development and use it to expose impure renders and missing cleanup.

misconceptions.text: Wrapping every function in useCallback and every value in useMemo makes an app faster.
useMemo guarantees the value will never be recomputed.
useCallback prevents a child from re-rendering by itself, even if the child is not memoised.

concepts.name: Hooks implementation model
concepts.summary: Evaluate code against the model that React stores hook state per component instance in call order, explaining why the rules of hooks exist.

concepts.name: Concurrent rendering and hook safety
concepts.summary: Assess how interruptible renders, transitions and deferred values constrain purity of render and effects.

concepts.name: Transitions and deferred values
concepts.summary: Judge when to mark updates as non-urgent with useTransition or useDeferredValue to keep interfaces responsive.

concepts.name: Custom hook API design
concepts.summary: Design custom hooks with stable return identities, clear contracts, composability and minimal dependency on call-site details.

concepts.name: Event-like effect patterns
concepts.summary: Create solutions that read the latest values inside effects without re-synchronising, using event-effect or latest-ref patterns.

concepts.name: Choosing state architecture
concepts.summary: Evaluate hooks-only state, reducers with context, server-state libraries and external stores for a given app's needs.

concepts.name: Testing and debugging hooks
concepts.summary: Evaluate strategies to test custom hooks and diagnose render loops, stale values and leaked effects using the profiler and devtools.

misconceptions.text: Hooks are magic and track state by variable name or by the component's source location.
useTransition makes the slow work itself run faster.
Effects can be made safe by simply omitting dependencies when a value should be read without re-running.
